past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If a loading truck has an output of 3600 J and its efficiency is 50%, then the input provided to the truck will be
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Efficiency = $(\text{Output Energy} / \text{Input Energy}) \times 100$. Rearranging for Input Energy: $\text{Input} = (\text{Output} / \text{Efficiency}) \times 100 = (3600 / 50) \times 100 = 7200\text{ J}$.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The kinetic energy of a 0.5 kg bullet moving with velocity of 500 m/s is
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Kinetic Energy ($KE$) = $\frac{1}{2} m v^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5\text{ kg} \times (500\text{ m/s})^2 = 0.25 \times 250000 = 62500\text{ J}$.

The given diagram shows three different blocks of insoluble material placed in three beakers that are partially filled with water.

Which of the given block(s) is/ are LESS denser than water?
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: An object floats partially above the liquid surface only when its average density is less than the density of the liquid. In the diagram, Block (2) floats at the top surface of the water, so Block (2) only has a density less than water.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: When the upthrust on a moving cargo ship becomes equal to its weight, then it will
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: By the principle of floatation, a body floats in equilibrium on a liquid whenever the upward buoyant force (upthrust) equals the downward weight of the body.

| Option | Atmospheric Pressure at Sea Level | Atmospheric Pressure on the Mountain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A | Low | High |
| B | Low | Low |
| C | High | High |
| D | High | Low |
options: A. Atmospheric Pressure at Sea Level: Low | Atmospheric Pressure on the Mountain: High
B. Atmospheric Pressure at Sea Level: Low | Atmospheric Pressure on the Mountain: Low
C. Atmospheric Pressure at Sea Level: High | Atmospheric Pressure on the Mountain: High
D. Atmospheric Pressure at Sea Level: High | Atmospheric Pressure on the Mountain: Low
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the air column above a surface. At sea level the air column is tallest and densest (High pressure), whereas on a mountain the air column above is shorter and less dense (Low pressure).

crqs.question: Explain why upthrust acts in the upward direction on an object immersed in a fluid.
crqs.answer: Hydrostatic pressure in a fluid increases with depth (P = ρgh). Consequently, the upward pressure on the bottom surface of an immersed object is greater than the downward pressure on its top surface, producing a net upward buoyant force (upthrust).
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I Model Paper II Q.7(b)(ii)

erqs.question: i. Explain why the walls of a dam filled with water are usually wedge-shaped. ii. If the density of water is 1,000 kg/m³, calculate the depth of water in a dam when the pressure at the bottom is 100,000 Pa (g = 9.8 m/s²).
erqs.answer: i. Liquid pressure increases with depth (P = ρgh), so water exerts a much larger lateral force near the bottom of the reservoir; a wider wedge-shaped base provides the structural strength to withstand this pressure. ii. Using P = ρgh: h = 100,000 / (1000 × 9.8) = 10.2 m.
erqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I 2025 Annual Paper II Q.7(b)

erqs.question:
The given figure shows the brake system of a vehicle.

i. Name the law which is used in the given brake system. (1 Mark)
ii. Calculate the pressure exerted by the liquid at G and H and the force that is applied at X. (5 Marks)
erqs.question_text:
The given figure shows the brake system of a vehicle.

i. Name the law which is used in the given brake system. (1 Mark)
ii. Calculate the pressure exerted by the liquid at G and H and the force that is applied at X. (5 Marks)

rubric.description: 1 mark for correctly identifying Pascal's law.
1 mark for calculating pressure at G: P_G = F₁ / A₁ = 1000 N / 2 m² = 500 N/m² (or 500 Pa).
1 mark for stating the pressure at H: P_H = 500 N/m² (or 500 Pa) because pressure is transmitted equally throughout an enclosed fluid.
1 mark for using the correct transmitted pressure value P = 500 N/m².
1 mark for writing the correct formula for force: F = P × A (or F₂ = P_H × A₂).
1 mark for calculating the correct force at X: F = 500 × 100 = 50,000 N.

erqs.answer:
**(i) Name of the law:**
The law used in the hydraulic brake system of a vehicle is **Pascal's law**.

**(ii) Pressure at G, Pressure at H, and Force at X:**
• **Pressure exerted at piston G ($P_G$):**
$P_G = \frac{\text{Force }(F_1)}{\text{Area }(A_1)} = \frac{1000\text{ N}}{2\text{ m}^2} = 500\text{ N/m}^2\text{ (or }500\text{ Pa)}$

• **Pressure exerted at piston H ($P_H$):**
According to Pascal's law, pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the liquid. Therefore:
$P_H = P_G = 500\text{ N/m}^2\text{ (or }500\text{ Pa)}$

• **Force applied at X ($F_2$):**
Since $P_H = \frac{F_2}{A_2}$:
$F_2 = P_H \times A_2 = 500\text{ N/m}^2 \times 100\text{ m}^2 = 50,000\text{ N}$.

numericals.problem: If the density of water is 1,000 kg/m3, then calculate the depth of water in a dam when the pressure at the bottom is 1,00,000 Pa. (Note: Take the value of acceleration due to gravity as 9.8 m/s2.)
numericals.solution:
Given data:
Density of water ($\rho$) = $1000 \text{ kg/m}^3$
Pressure ($P$) = $100,000 \text{ Pa}$
Acceleration due to gravity ($g$) = $9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$

Formula:
$P = \rho g h$

Calculation:
$100,000 = 1000 \times 9.8 \times h$
$100,000 = 9800 \times h$
$h = \frac{100,000}{9800}$
$h \approx 10.2$ m
